# Task: CAL-7207 — Fix pinned chat ordering and add drag-and-drop reordering

(Brief = the Notion ticket, verbatim. Repo: called-deeweb at develop@1f680c659. Same text Claude received.)

## Story
Pinned chats in the chat list don't hold their order. The backend stores an order number for every pinned channel and the frontend sorts by that number, so the display side is working correctly. The issue is on write, pinning and unpinning never renumber the stored orders. Unpinning leaves gaps in the sequence, and pinning assigns the new order based on the array length, so numbers collide and new pins can land above older ones.
Users also have no way to rearrange their pinned chats. Rather than leaving drag handles visible all the time, which makes the list noisy, pinned editing goes behind an explicit edit mode. An Edit button sits in the empty right half of the PINNED heading. Turning it on puts a checkbox on every row so you can pin and unpin in bulk, shows a drag handle on the pinned rows, and gives you Save and Cancel. Turning it off puts the list back to normal.

## Tasks
- Renumber pinnedChannels densely (order = index) on every write: pin, unpin, and removeChannelFromPinned
- Fix the onUserJoined insert so an unpinned channel can never land above the pinned block
- Add an Edit / Done button to the right side of the PINNED heading
- Build the edit-mode row: checkbox, avatar, name, drag handle. Avatars stay so near-identical names stay tellable apart
- Check and uncheck to pin and unpin, with the row moving between PINNED and ALL CHATS as feedback
- Drag to reorder the pinned rows, with a 44px handle so it is a real touch target
- Save writes the whole renumbered array in one request, Cancel throws the draft away
- Remove the always-visible drag handles
- Keyboard reorder and screen reader announcements on the handle
- Unit tests for the ordering helpers, the pin and unpin writes, and the edit-mode save and cancel

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pinned chats always render in the backend-stored order, stable across refetches
- Pinning a new chat adds it to the end of the pinned section, never above older pins
- Unpinning (including channel delete or leave) keeps the remaining pins in their existing order
- Drag handles are not visible until the user turns on Edit
- In edit mode the user can check and uncheck chats to pin them, and drag pinned chats to reorder
- Save persists both the new pin set and the new order in one request, and the order survives a reload
- Cancel leaves the pinned chats exactly as they were
- Outside edit mode, rows still open the chat on click
- The drag handle is reachable and operable by keyboard

## Notes
- The read path is correct: ContactList/index.tsx sorts pinned channels by the stored order number
- The write path is the bug: handlePinChannel in ChannelMenu.tsx. Unpin filters the entry out without renumbering the rest. Pin assigns the new order from pinnedChannels.length, a count, not max order plus one
- Example: pin A, B, C, D giving orders 0 to 3. Unpin A and C, leaving D at 3. The next two pins get orders 1 and 2, so both sort above D even though D was pinned first
- The same missing renumber exists in removeChannelFromPinned in ContactList/index.tsx, which runs when a channel is deleted or the user leaves it
- Smaller related issue: the onUserJoined handler in ContactList/index.tsx can insert an unpinned channel above the whole pinned block when the last pinned channel is not in the loaded list yet
- Fix direction: renumber the whole array densely (order equals index) on every write. PATCH /v1/account/settings replaces the full pinnedChannels array, so a save is a single mutation
- For drag-and-drop: @dnd-kit is already installed. The Pathway board has a working sortable pattern to copy (usePhaseReordering.ts, PathwayDragDropContext.tsx). Use a drag handle so rows stay clickable to open the chat
- Edit mode keeps the avatar. On a pinned row the avatar costs no height at all, because the 44px handle touch target already sets the row height. The sidebar minimum width is 320px and the name still gets about 154px next to the checkbox, avatar and handle
- Keeping avatars matters because names repeat in the real list. There are two Bethany University rows and two Agents rows on the test account
- The pinned heading only renders when there is at least one pin, so the first pin still has to come from the existing right-click Pin Channel action. Do not remove it

## Suggested scripted follow-ups (Jason drives; use or ignore)
T2: "Fix the ordering bug first, with tests, before any UI work."
T3: "Now the edit mode UX."
T4: "Save must be one request; the handle must be keyboard-operable and 44px; drag handles only in edit mode."
T5: "Run the suite and make it green."
T6: "Edit mode must close automatically when a search starts (search hides the pinned section)."

## Project Overview

Called-deeweb is a monorepo containing a React-based chat application deployed as a PWA and as iOS and Android apps via Capacitor. It uses a monorepo structure with workspaces for apps and packages.

## Architecture

- **Main Application**: `apps/called-chat` - Primary React chat application
- **Packages**:
  - `called-api` - OpenAPI-generated TypeScript types and API client
  - `called-common` - Shared components and utilities

## Development Commands

### Root Level Commands
```bash
# Run tests - Always from the root of the project never from called-chat
npm run test

# Run tests with coverage
npm run test:coverage

# Install all dependencies across workspaces
npm install

# Setup pre-commit hooks (if they don't work)
npm run prepare

# Run pre-push hooks across all workspaces
npm run pre-push
```

### App Development (apps/called-chat)
```bash
# Development with API sync
npm run dev

# Build for production
npm run build

# Lint JavaScript/TypeScript
npm run lint:js

# Lint styles
npm run lint:styles

# Fix linting issues
npm run lint:fix

# Sync API types from OpenAPI spec
npm run sync-api

# Clean build artifacts and sync API
npm run clean:sync
```

## Code Style and Guidelines

### Component Structure
Follow this import order and component structure:
```typescript
// Import global packages first (React hooks, third-party libs)
import { [HOOKS], [EVENT_TYPES] } from 'react';
import { [COMPONENTS] } from '[LIBS]';

// Import project-related packages next
import [ASSETS] from '[PROJECT_PATH]';

// Import local components outside current directory
import { [LOCAL_COMPONENTS] } from '[LOCAL_PATH]';

// Import same/nested directory files
import { [LOCAL_FILES] } from './[FILE]';

// Import local styles last, with line break
import styles from './[COMPONENT].module.scss';

// Props interface: ComponentNameProps
interface [COMPONENT]Props {
    [PROP]: [TYPE];
}

// Export component, destructure props
export const [COMPONENT] = ({ [PROP] }: [COMPONENT]Props) => {
    // Hooks and state, always defined before use
    const [VAR] = [HOOK]();

    // Effects
    useEffect(() => {
        // [EFFECT_LOGIC]
    }, []);

    // Handlers: handle[EVENT]
    const handle[EVENT] = () => {
        // [HANDLER_LOGIC]
    };

    // JSX return
    return (
        <[ELEMENT] className={styles.[CLASS]}>
            {/* Content */}
        </[ELEMENT]>
    );
};
```

### Key Requirements
- Use 4-space indentation
- Never use Tailwind classes; use SCSS modules
- Never use Material UI Paper or Box components; use simple divs
- Event handlers must use "handle" prefix
- Always use TypeScript `interface` (not `type`) for component props and object shapes; avoid 'any' types

- **React Query**: For server state and data fetching

### Routing

### Styling

- **CSS Custom Properties**: Use design system variables for colors and typography

  --web-sm-semibold
  --web-base-medium

  --web-xl-medium
  --web-xl-semibold
  --web-2x-semibold
  --web-3x-semibold
  --web-4x-medium

  Example: For 16px semibold, use font: var(--web-base-medium);.

  - For colors, always use alias variables (never direct color names or hex codes inline). Key categories and examples:
  - Brand/Accent: --brand (var(--purple-heart)), --bg-accent-1 (var(--blue-chalk)), --text-brand-default (var(--purple-heart)).

  - Text: --text-default (var(--shark)), --text-weak (var(--cadet-blue)), --text-strong (var(--woodsmoke)), --text-disabled (var(--dolphin)).

  - Component-Specific: --event-boost-polls-bg-default (var(--blue-gem-2)), --announcement-boost-bg-default (var(--cornflower-blue)).
  Refer to full alias list if needed, but prioritize aliases for consistency.

## API Integration

The project uses OpenAPI code generation:

Repo: called-deeweb at develop@1f680c659. Same text Claude received.)█## Story█Pinned chats in the chat list don't hold their order. The backend stores an order number for every pinned channel and the frontend sorts by that number, so the display side is working correctly. The issue is on write, pinning and unpinning never renumber the stored orders. Unpinning leaves gaps in the sequence, and pinning assigns the new order based on the array length, so numbers collide and new pins can land above older ones.█Users also have no way to rearrange their pinned chats. Rather than leaving drag handles visible all the time, which makes the list noisy, pinned editing goes behind an explicit edit mode. An Edit button sits in the empty right half of the PINNED heading. Turning it on puts a checkbox on every row so you can pin and unpin in bulk, shows a drag handle on the pinned rows, and gives you Save and Cancel. Turning it off puts the list back to normal.█## Tasks█- Renumber pinnedChannels densely (order = index) on every write: pin, unpin, and removeChannelFromPinned█- Fix the onUserJoined insert so an unpinned channel can never land above the pinned block█- Add an Edit / Done button to the right side of the PINNED heading█- Build the edit-mode row: checkbox, avatar, name, drag handle. Avatars stay so near-identical names stay tellable apart█- Check and uncheck to pin and unpin, with the row moving between PINNED and ALL CHATS as feedback█- Drag to reorder the pinned rows, with a 44px handle so it is a real touch target█- Save writes the whole renumbered array in one request, Cancel throws the draft away█- Remove the always-visible drag handles█- Keyboard reorder and screen reader announcements on the handle█- Unit tests for the ordering helpers, the pin and unpin writes, and the edit-mode save and cancel█## Acceptance Criteria█- Pinned chats always render in the backend-stored order, stable across refetches█- Pinning a new chat adds it to the end of the pinned section, never above older pins█- Unpinning (including channel delete or leave) keeps the remaining pins in their existing order█- Drag handles are not visible until the user turns on Edit█- In edit mode the user can check and uncheck chats to pin them, and drag pinned chats to reorder█- Save persists both the new pin set and the new order in one request, and the order survives a reload█- Cancel leaves the pinned chats exactly as they were█- Outside edit mode, rows still open the chat on click█- The drag handle is reachable and operable by keyboard█## Notes█- The read path is correct: ContactList/index.tsx sorts pinned channels by the stored order number█- The write path is the bug: handlePinChannel in ChannelMenu.tsx. Unpin filters the entry out without renumbering the rest. Pin assigns the new order from pinnedChannels.length, a count, not max order plus one█- Example: pin A, B, C, D giving orders 0 to 3. Unpin A and C, leaving D at 3. The next two pins get orders 1 and 2, so both sort above D even though D was pinned first█- The same missing renumber exists in removeChannelFromPinned in ContactList/index.tsx, which runs when a channel is deleted or the user leaves it█- Smaller related issue: the onUserJoined handler in ContactList/index.tsx can insert an unpinned channel above the whole pinned block when the last pinned channel is not in the loaded list yet█- Fix direction: renumber the whole array densely (order equals index) on every write. PATCH /v1/account/settings replaces the full pinnedChannels array, so a save is a single mutation█- For drag-and-drop: @dnd-kit is already installed. The Pathway board has a working sortable pattern to copy (usePhaseReordering.ts, PathwayDragDropContext.tsx). Use a drag handle so rows stay clickable to open the chat█- Edit mode keeps the avatar. On a pinned row the avatar costs no height at all, because the 44px handle touch target already sets the row height. The sidebar minimum width is 320px and the name still gets about 154px next to the checkbox, avatar and handle█- Keeping avatars matters because names repeat in the real list. # CAL-7207 - Fix pinned chat ordering + drag-and-drop reordering

- Branch: ab/qwen-cal7207 (develop@1f680c659)
- Notion: see implementation-prompt (D:\dev\ab-tasks\_runs\deeweb\qwen\implementation-prompt.txt)

## Diagnosis

- Read path is correct: ContactList sorts pinned rows by `order`.
- Write path is broken:
  - `ChannelMenu.handlePinChannel` pin assigns `order: pinnedChannels.length` (a count, not max+1); unpin filters without renumbering → gaps → new pins sort above older ones.
  - `ContactList.removeChannelFromPinned` (delete/leave) has the same missing renumber.
  - `onUserJoined` splices a new channel after the last *stored* pin, but that pin may not be in the loaded list → `lastPinnedIndex = -1` → new channel lands at index 0, above the whole pinned block.
- "Remove always-visible drag handles": no drag handle exists in current code — the new handle must only appear in edit mode.

## Design

- New pure helpers in `apps/called-chat/src/utils/pinnedChannels.ts`:
  - `renumberPinnedChannels(pins)` — sort by stored order, renumber densely (order = index).
  - `addPinnedChannel(pins, url)` — dedupe, append, renumber → new pin always lands at the end.
  - `removePinnedChannel(pins, url)` — filter, renumber densely.
  - `toPinnedChannels(urls)` — dense 0..n from an ordered url list (edit-mode save).
- New hook `ContactList/usePinnedChannelsEdit.ts` — edit-mode state machine:
  - draft url list; start (seed from saved pins), cancel (discard, no write), save (single PATCH `toPinnedChannels(draft)`, exit on success, stay + snackbar on failure), toggle, reorder (arrayMove), drop (server-side delete/leave prunes draft too).
- `ChannelMenu.handlePinChannel` → add/remove helpers; every write renumbers densely.
- `ContactList/index.tsx`:
  - `effectivePinnedChannels = isEditing ? draft : savedPins` drives sort, onUserJoined boundary, delete/leave checks, filtered pinned section.
  - onUserJoined: anchor on the last pin actually *present* in the loaded list → new channel can't land above the pinned block.
  - `removeChannelFromPinned` uses helper (server write) + prunes draft.
  - PINNED heading right side: [Edit] normally; in edit mode [Cancel] [Done] (Done = save). Heading always renders in edit mode so there is always an exit path even when the draft empties.
  - T6: edit mode auto-closes when a search becomes active.
  - Save = one `patchSettings` (mutateAsync) + settings-query invalidation.
- `ChannelList.tsx` edit mode:
  - Pinned block wrapped in `DndContext` (Pointer + Keyboard sensors, sortableKeyboardCoordinates) + `SortableContext`; rows = `SortableChannelRow` → `ChannelEditRow` (checkbox, 40px avatar, name, 44px DotsSixVertical handle with useSortable attributes/listeners).
  - Unpinned rows = `ChannelEditRow` without handle.
  - Rows are no longer chat-opening buttons in edit mode (normal mode unchanged).
- 44px handle = row height; avatar costs no extra height (matches ticket math at 320px sidebar).

- [x] T2: `usePinnedChannelsEdit` hook + tests (save = one dense write + exit; cancel = no write; failure = stay in edit)
